title: AI Gameplan Week 3: Real Projects
tagline: Do real work. Use agents, research, data, and reporting on business tasks that matter.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Agent Delegation

video.title: AI Agents Explained Simply
video.purpose: Understand what AI agents are and how they work before you start delegating to them.

lessons.goal: You learn how to split work between yourself, AI chat, and an agent.
sections: Write the goal, context, constraints, and proof needed.

Quick check: are you using Claude in the browser, saving to Google Drive, and keeping your AI Workspace folder organized? This week involves real tasks. If you need to install anything new, check with CJ first. Browser tools and cloud storage come first.
Decide what You do, what Claude drafts, what Codex checks, and what an agent can research.
No private info, no public action, verify before reporting.
Turn in one delegation plan for a real CJ task.

quiz.q: What should an agent not do without approval?

lessons.checkpoint: I can show proof for agent delegation.

visuals.title: Agent delegation map
visuals.note: Split work by risk, proof, and owner.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Business Admin Workflow
lessons.goal: You build a simple admin workflow for a real business task.
sections: Choose invoice tracking, camp list cleanup, lead follow up, schedule prep, or folder organization.
Write current steps, pain points, and what good looks like.
Use AI to draft a checklist or SOP. You edit it for reality.
Turn in the workflow, checklist, and proof that it can be followed.

choices: A repeatable checklist for doing the job
It saves time and reduces misses

lessons.checkpoint: I can show proof for business admin workflow.

visuals.title: Admin workflow
visuals.note: A simple checklist can save CJ hours when it is real.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Research Report

video.title: How I Use AI Tools to 10x My Productivity
video.purpose: See how AI tools are used for research and productivity in real workflows.

lessons.goal: You learn to research with sources, not guesses.
sections: Turn the topic into one clear question and 3 sub questions.
Use official pages first, then credible support sources.
Record title, link, date checked, and why it matters.
Turn in a 1 to 2 page research report with source log.

quiz.q: What belongs in a source log?
choices: Title, link, date checked, why it matters

lessons.checkpoint: I can show proof for research report.

visuals.title: Research source log
visuals.note: Every claim needs a source CJ can check.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Data and Reporting

video.title: How to Write an Executive Summary
video.purpose: Learn how to turn data into a clear, short summary that decision makers can act on.

lessons.goal: You turn a small dataset or report into an executive summary.
sections: Use a safe sample report, campaign numbers CJ provides, or public stats.
Identify what changed, what matters, and what question remains.
Use plain language: what happened, why it matters, what to do next.
Turn in one page with 3 insights, 3 risks, and 3 next actions.

quiz.q: What should a report answer first?
choices: What happened and why it matters
A useful pattern from the data

quiz.q: What should you do with unknowns?

lessons.checkpoint: I can show proof for data and reporting.

visuals.title: Executive summary
visuals.note: Short, clear, useful. No data dump.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: CJ Backlog Project
lessons.goal: You complete one assigned real project from CJ backlog with a clean closeout.
sections: Write the goal, due date, owner, files, and proof before starting.
If blocked for 30 minutes, write the exact blocker and ask CJ.
Turn in the finished work, proof, Drive location, and closeout note.

quiz.q: What should you do before starting backlog work?

choices: After 30 minutes blocked with a clear question

quiz.q: What proves the project is done?
choices: Finished work, location, proof, and closeout

lessons.checkpoint: I can show proof for cj backlog project.

visuals.title: Real project closeout
visuals.note: The work is not done until CJ can find it and review it.

qualityRules: Real work must have a written goal before execution.
Every claim in research needs a source.
Every report needs next actions, not just numbers.
Every project needs a closeout note.
Cloud first: browser tools and cloud storage before any installs. Check with CJ before installing anything new.
